briefs.headline: Coforge hires Egon Zehnder to find two independent directors
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Coforge has appointed global executive search firm Egon Zehnder to identify two additional independent directors as the company moves to strengthen its board, following the resignations of chairman OP Bhatt and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh. The board said the governance issues that led to the exits had no impact on the company's operations, financial reporting or business outlook. Board members also said there was no dissent among them. Independent director Beth Boucher has been appointed NRC chair.
Interim chair Vivek Sharma said the search would be global, focusing on candidates with governance experience, professional expertise and strategic perspectives to strengthen the board and support Coforge's long-term growth. Sharma will also oversee the process to elect a permanent chair but said he would not be a candidate for the role.
The board detailed the findings of an internal audit that preceded the resignations. KPMG, Coforge's internal auditor, reviewed the accuracy of board reporting as part of its FY27 audit plan. The audit found that board evaluation reports were available only to the then NRC chair and chairman, and were not shared with other board members.
"The manner in which the evaluation findings were presented without sharing copies of report by chairman of board and NRC chair did not cover all relevant aspects of the findings," said John Speight, president and executive director, in an investor call on Monday.

briefs.headline: Essar arm to buy UK fuel retailer for nearly $550 million
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Essar Energy Transition's retail arm has agreed to acquire independent UK forecourt operator SGN Retail in a deal estimated at about 400 million pounds ($540 million or Rs 5,166 crore), adding 118 sites to its network and creating a 235-site estate as it seeks to build a vertically integrated fuel business in Britain.
EET Retail, the retail division of Essar Energy Transition Fuels, in a statement said it had agreed to acquire 100% of SGN Retail, which was founded by Graham Peacock and Susan Tobbell.
While the company did not disclose the financial details, sources said the deal is estimated to be about 400 million pounds. The deal will give EET Retail annual fuel throughput of more than 650 million litres, combining SGN Retail's 118 locations with the 117 sites already operated by EET Retail.
EET Retail said the enlarged network would make it the UK's second-largest forecourt operator with direct integration into fuel production. It plans to expand the network to about 800 sites by 2031, equivalent to roughly 9% of the UK market, with fuel supplied by Essar's Stanlow refinery in Cheshire.
"Building a scaled, vertically integrated retail forecourt platform is a critical pillar of our long-term UK strategy. 
SGN Retail is one of the highest-quality forecourt networks in the UK well ahead of the market. This acquisition accelerates our plan to build a nationwide, vertically integrated platform of 800 sites, backed by direct refinery supply and delivering competitive prices at the pump for UK motorists," said Arvan Ruia, CEO of EET Retail.
The acquisition comes as EET seeks to reconnect fuel production with retail distribution, arguing that the UK's fuel market has become increasingly fragmented over the past two decades as oil majors reduced investment in domestic refining.
EET said the model would allow fuel refined at Stanlow to be distributed more directly to its own forecourts, reducing reliance on imports and multiple layers in the domestic supply chain. "This is a unique, best-in-class opportunity and advances a core part of our M&A strategy. The transaction is backed by a top-tier group of banks spanning four continents, several supporting the UK forecourt sector for the first time, underscoring confidence in our backward-integrated growth model and in the UK fuels and convenience markets," said Viral Gathani, head of strategic transactions at Essar Energy Transition (EET).
The transaction is being financed through a combination of cash and a new 250 million pound senior debt facility arranged by First Abu Dhabi Bank, Macquarie Bank, Mizrahi Tefahot Bank, Natixis, OakNorth Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, and others. Agencies

briefs.headline: Amazon's quick commerce business crosses $1 billion in gross annualised sales
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Amazon's quick commerce business has now crossed $1 billion in gross annualised sales in India over the past three-month period and has caught up with competition to become one of the top three market players in Delhi and Bengaluru, despite a late entry into the instant delivery space, a top company executive said.
In an interview, Amazon's India country manager Samir Kumar said the growth has come on the back of orders doubling every quarter. A big push has also come from Prime customers, who end up shopping about three times more on Amazon Now. "Prime is a big driver for our flywheel but even non-prime customers are coming in quite a good number. As we start reaching smaller cities, we are also seeing a very, very healthy growth in non-Prime customers. They are also converting to Prime," Kumar said.
Gross annualised sales is typically calculated by taking the total gross sales for a month or a quarter and multiplying it to project a full 12-month period. It reflects the value of orders placed minus discounts, cancellations and excluding GST.
Amazon Now officially started operations in March quarter last year, about four months after launch of Flipkart's Minutes and having ceded much of the market share to Eternal's Blinkit, Swiggy's Instamart and Zepto. 
In what seems as a clear mandate from Amazon's Seattle headquarters to scale up Now's execution on ground here, the firm's top boss Andy Jassy on a visit to India earlier this year said Now will expand to over 300 cities and build the largest delivery-in-minutes network. It was Jassy's first India tour since assuming office in 2021. By Diwali, Now will be scaled to 100 cities and to 1,000 dark stores by year-end. Sources said Now's orders stand at about 700,000 per day. In all, it has gained market share of about 10% by orders and about 14% by value.
"Our growth engine is still going to be a lot more penetrating into smaller cities and towns," Kumar said. About 70% of Amazon's (overall) customers come from smaller cities. The company has taken Now to cities such as Udupi, Warangal, Guntur and plans are afoot to launch it in places like Kapurthala and Gurdaspur going ahead. Now will have a play across both mass and premium price points and Kumar's target is to widen the selection of products and categories on the platform. "Our focus will be on whether we can serve a customer need in minutes in a sustainable and safe way," Kumar said.

briefs.headline: Solar Industries acquires South African company for 13,000 crore
briefs.deck: To Create One Of World's Most Integrated & Largest Blasting Solutions Player With Omnia
briefs.bodyText:
Nagpur: Solar Industries, a Nagpur-headquartered explosives manufacturer, has signed a definitive agreement to take over South Africa's Omnia Holdings in a Rs 12,951 crore deal, leading to formation of one of the world's largest and most integrated blasting solutions platform.
Solar would also get access to key international markets, including US, Canada, Australia, Brazil and Indonesia, apart from southern and western Africa through Omnia's network. The buyout will enable Solar Group to get a foothold in the farm sector too. Omnia is a major manufacturer of ammonium nitrate, which is used in agriculture and explosives sectors.
To get a foothold in farm sector
The buyout is expected to be completed in early-to mid-2027, subject to customary conditions, including competition approvals in relevant jurisdictions. After completion, Omnia will be delisted from Johannesburg Stock Exchange and A2X Markets, the company said in a regulatory filing. The proposed transaction marks a transformational milestone in Solar Group's strategic ambition to become leading global explosives and mining solutions provider, the company said.
Johannesburg-based Omnia operates in 23 countries, while it reaches out to 40 nations through a network of 70 distribution centres, clocking a turnover of $1.4 billion (Rs 13,307 crore) for the fiscal ending March 2026, compared with $1.3 billion in FY25 and $1.2 billion in FY24, and has remained cash positive, stated a Solar Group representative.
The buyout will take place through Solar SA Investments Proprietary, a wholly owned subsidiary of Solar Industries. This is the second South African takeover by Solar Group in the recent past. In 2024, it acquired ProBlast, a local South African company specialising in open cast mining, drilling, blasting and explosive services. Omnia's agriculture segment operates nitric acid and ammonium nitrate production facilities, which are the largest and most reliable in the region, said a note.
"Omnia is a business we long admired for the strength of its mining and agriculture businesses' differentiated technology, brands and deep customer relationships. The proposed transaction marks an important milestone in our ambition to become a global leader in explosives and blasting solutions, while providing us a meaningful entry into the integrated crop nutrition and biological solutions," said Solar Group's MD Manish Nuwal.
Omnia's BME brand brings a strong international mining platform, high-quality assets, technological leadership in electronic initiation and integrated ammonium nitrate manufacturing facility, said Nuwal. Solar Group has steadily expanded its footprint across Africa. It first entered the South African Development Community (SDAC) region in 2010 by establishing a manufacturing facility at Zambia in 2010.

briefs.headline: 4 buyers paid Rs 2.08 crore each for flats, but pool, spa, gym missing; RERA orders Rs 10 lakh
briefs.deck: A reputed builder has been asked to pay Rs 10 lakh compensation to four homebuyers after a joint inspection and photographs showed that several amenities promised in the project, including a senior citizen park, open gym, spa, amphitheatre and sports facilities, had not been delivered.
briefs.bodyText:
A builder promises several amenities in a housing project, but fails to deliver. What happens after that? A Karnataka RERA ruling in this context assumes importance.
A reputed builder has been asked to pay Rs 10 lakh compensation to four homebuyers after a joint inspection and photographs showed that several amenities promised in the project, including a senior citizen park, open gym, spa, amphitheatre and sports facilities, had not been delivered.
The authority held that showcasing these facilities in brochures and agreements but failing to provide them amounted to misrepresentation, despite the buyers having signed the sale deeds.
What the case is about
The order followed a complaint filed by four homebuyers. Their housing project is situated in Bangalore North. The buyers had purchased flats in the project for Rs 2.08 crore each and executed the sale deeds in 2022. At the time of purchase, the builder had committed to providing a range of amenities. However, the promised facilities were not constructed.
The Karnataka RERA tribunal in Bangalore has directed the to pay Rs 10 lakh in compensation to four homebuyers after photographic evidence established that several amenities promised to them had not been provided. These included a senior citizen park, open gym, spa, open amphitheatre, badminton court and other facilities.
On September 4, 2026, the Karnataka RERA authority held that the builder had presented the buyers with colourful dreams by featuring the promised amenities in the project brochure, allotment letters and agreements.
The authority observed that the failure to deliver those commitments, even if it was not intentional, amounted to misrepresentation. K-RERA consequently ordered the builder to pay Rs 10 lakh as compensation to the four homebuyers.
Karnataka RERA discussion
Smt Maheshwari S Hiremath, adjudicating officer of Karnataka RERA, heard the case.
BIAAPA has not yet released the final order, so builder has no obligation to construct the club house
Under Clause 12.1 of the sale agreement, the builder is required to complete the club house within 18 months from the date on which BIAAPA issues the site release order. In this case, however, BIAAPA has issued only a partial release order.
Karnataka RERA therefore held that the builder cannot, at this stage, be held responsible for failing to hand over a fully completed club house.
Joint inspection photographs show several amenities remain incomplete
A joint inspection of the project was conducted by the homebuyers and the builder on May 14, 2026, in accordance with the court's order. The inspection was accompanied by several photographs documenting the condition of the premises.
Although the builder's representatives attended the inspection, they did not sign the joint inspection report. However, the colour photographs taken during the inspection established their presence at the project premises.
Karnataka RERA noted that purchasing a home is generally a long-held aspiration for buyers, who may put their lifetime savings into the purchase and take loans that can take years to repay. Against this backdrop, the authority said a builder has a responsibility to honour that aspiration rather than leave homebuyers running from pillar to post.
The authority further referred to Section 12 of the 
RERA Act
, under which a builder is responsible for the veracity of representations made in an advertisement or prospectus. Accordingly, the builder is bound to provide the amenities promised in the advertisement or prospectus for the particular project.
In the present case, although the builder executed the sale deed in 2022, the amenities that had been promised to the buyers had still not been fully provided.
Karnataka RERA observed: “Mere execution of a sale deed in favour of the allottee is not sufficient without completion of the project by providing all amenities /facilities as agreed.”
The authority said the builder is required to complete the project in all respects, particularly since the homebuyers had pointed out that several amenities remained incomplete or had not been constructed.
The authority also noted several other deficiencies at the project. These included portions of the compound wall that were missing, a borewell that had been dug in a private area, and inadequate maintenance of the STP and WTP, which was resulting in bad smells, among other issues.
The coloured photographs taken during the joint inspection documented these conditions and were captured in the presence of the builder's representative while the inspection report was being prepared.
Karnataka RERA observed: “Perused all colored photographs which goes to show that several amenities are incomplete such as compound wall, SBR tanks 1 and 2, club house, sewage collection tank, STP and WTP plant room, gate at the entrance, no salt or brine used for water treatment, STP chambers are open, etc.”
At the same time, the photographs indicated that some facilities, including the children's play area, park and yoga deck, had been completed.
Based on its findings, the K-RERA authority directed the builder to pay Rs 10 lakh as compensation within 60 days. If the amount is not paid within the stipulated period, the builder will also be required to pay interest on the compensation.
How did the homebuyers win?
Asha Kiran Sharma, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the Karnataka RERA order serves as an important reminder that developers cannot rely on contractual wording to escape responsibility when promised facilities are not delivered.
Sharma said the significant aspect of the case was that the builder attempted to shift the focus towards documentation rather than the actual facilities that formed part of the homebuyers' purchase. According to her, the promised pool, gym, spa and other amenities were not constructed, a fact established during a joint inspection conducted in May 2026.
The joint inspection report, which was carried out under the direction of K-RERA, further recorded that the project did not have a children's play area, badminton or tennis court or open gym. It also found that the clubhouse did not have the promised pool, spa, guest rooms and indoor games area.
The builder's own staff attended the inspection and were also visible in the photographs taken during the exercise, leaving little scope for a claim that the inspection findings were inaccurate.
Sharma said the ruling also carries an important message for builders. A developer cannot prepare a sale deed declaring its obligations to be fulfilled and later rely on that same document to defend itself against claims concerning facilities it had promised. The Karnataka RERA Authority noted that such documents are one-sided instruments prepared entirely by the builder, while buyers frequently have little practical choice other than signing them.
For homebuyers, Sharma said the order provides reassurance that an honest and genuine error, such as mentioning an incorrect project registration number, will not by itself defeat an otherwise legitimate complaint. What matters is that the project and the amenities that were promised can be clearly established from the available record.
Sharma says: "At the end of the day, people don't pour their life savings and years of loan repayments into a home just to get a bare plot with a signature on a deed. They're buying into a lifestyle that was promised to them in a brochure, and this order says quite plainly that promoters have to be held to that promise, not just to the transaction on paper."

briefs.headline: Maruti Suzuki achieves one lakh units of Jimmy, FRONX, e VITARA exports to Japan
briefs.deck: Exports of FRONX to Japan commenced in August 2024, followed by Jimny 5-door in December 2024. The Company’s first Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV), e VITARA, joined this export portfolio in September 2025
briefs.bodyText:
Maruti Suzuki India Ltd said it has achieved one lakh units of cumulative exports of Made-in-India Jimny 5-door, FRONX and e VITARA to Japan considered one of the world’s most competitive and advanced automobile markets.
Exports of FRONX to Japan commenced in August 2024, followed by Jimny 5-door in December 2024. The Company’s first Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV), e VITARA, joined this export portfolio in September 2025.

Japan is now Maruti Suzuki’s second-largest export market by volume. Maruti Suzuki-manufactured vehicles accounted for nearly 100% of imports by Suzuki in Japan during FY26, the company said.
Hisashi Takeuchi, managing director & CEO, Maruti Suzuki India said, “The milestone of over 1 lakh exports of Jimny 5-door, FRONX, and e VITARA to Japan is a powerful endorsement of India’s manufacturing excellence.”
“This achievement is particularly significant as Japan is one of the world’s most demanding and advanced automobile markets. The export milestone also symbolises the remarkable evolution of the India-Japan partnership,” he said.
“What began as Suzuki’s vision to manufacture automobiles in India has come full circle, with Made-in-India vehicles finding strong acceptance among Japanese customers. This success has helped Japan emerge as the second biggest market for Maruti Suzuki exports,” he added.

briefs.headline: India approves expedited export of electricity to flood-hit Nepal
briefs.deck: “The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and longstanding energy cooperation between India and Nepal,” stated India’s Power Ministry.
briefs.bodyText:
India’s Ministry of Power have given their go-ahead for exporting power to Nepal to help recover from devastating floods which, among other things, destroyed their hydropower infrastructure and took lives of more than 1,300 people.
The approval paves the way for exporting power for 18 hours a day starting Sept 13 until Dec 31 this year.
“The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and longstanding energy cooperation between India and Nepal,” stated India’s Power Ministry.
It further informed the quantum of power to be exported from January next year would be reviewed in December.
The Hindu had earlier reported that Kathmandu had asked New Delhi to accord requisite approvals for transmission of electricity earlier than usual.
Nepal usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, starting around October, as power generation is typically low in the Himalayan country during the freezing winter months.
Conversely, the country exports its excess hydropower to India during the summer.
According to official data, India imported 3,299 million units (MUs) of power from Nepal in fiscal year 2025-26 and exported 1,451 MUs to it.

stories.headline: 'The mistakes I made, I won't make again': Animesh Kujur ready for Asian Games
stories.deck: Animesh Kujur arrives in Aichi-Nagoya with a 10.14 personal best in the 100m and the national 200m record of 20.32. He has gained confidence from international competitions, learned how to manage his body, when to peak and when to reduce the load. With strong Asian competition ahead, including Japan's Shuhei Tada and Soshi Mizukubo, Kujur believes his Asian Championships mistakes will not be…
stories.bodyText:
By the time Animesh Kujur lined up for the 200m at the Indian Athletics Series Final at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi last week, the instruction from his coach was fairly simple: don't chase the clock.
It was getting late. The priority was to stay injury-free, execute the bend and finish the race.
Kujur won in 20.59 seconds after winning the 100m in 10.21 seconds. Gurindervir Singh, India's 100m national record holder, was second in 10.32.
The meeting was the final domestic stop before the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. For Kujur, the two victories were less about producing another headline time than getting through the evening and into the final phase of his preparation.
“The coach said that the time is getting late, so just stay injury-free. Don't push too much. Just try to come first,” Kujur told TimesofIndia.com after the race. “Just try to execute the curve. That's it. And I just did it like that. I came straight and just maintained my pace. And just finished the race.”
He arrives in Aichi-Nagoya with a 10.14 personal best in the 100m and the national 200m record of 20.32, set at the 2025 Asian Championships. 
He will compete in the 100m, 200m and relay.
The 10.14 came in Wetzlar, Germany, in July and remains the second-fastest 100m by an Indian, behind Gurindervir's 10.09 national record. Kujur's run was also the fastest 100m by an Indian outside the country.
Animesh Kujur (Image credit: Special arrangement)
Gurindervir's 10.09 came at the Federation Cup in Ranchi in May, when the Indian record changed hands repeatedly over a short period. Kujur had run 10.15 before Gurindervir reclaimed the record with 10.09.
The two have continued to race each other through the season. At the Series Final in Delhi, Kujur had the better of the two again.
Kujur said that competition has changed the way he feels about the 100m.
“I will say 100, I am having more fun now because I am getting competition from Guri again and again,” he said.
He does not feel the same level of competition in the 200m.
“In 200, there is not as much competition as there should be in India,” he said. “But when you get competition, that is when you enjoy running fast.”
The Asian Games will give him plenty of it.
A tougher sprint field awaits in Aichi-Nagoya
Japan's Shuhei Tada and Yuki Koike are listed for the men's 100m. Tada has a 10.01 personal best, while Koike has run 10.06. Both are part of Japan's Asian Games sprint team.
The wider Asian field has also produced several sub-10.10-level performances this season, with Japan's Rikuto Higuchi at 10.01 and other Japanese sprinters around the 10.03-10.04 mark. Gurindervir's 10.09 and Kujur's 10.14 put the Indian pair firmly in that group.
The 200m is an even tougher proposition on paper.
Japan's Soshi Mizukubo has run 20.07 this season and won the Japanese national title. Thailand's Puripol Boonson has gone 20.03, a national record, while Kujur's Indian record remains 20.32.
Kujur's own 2026 200m season has been less spectacular than his record-breaking 2025, but that has not altered how he sees the event.
Earlier in the year, he qualified for the Asian Games with 20.74 at the National Inter-State Championships, a time comfortably inside the qualification mark but well outside his 20.32 national record.
The clock is no longer driving Kujur's races
He has since been thinking less about producing a particular time in every race.
In 2024, Kujur said, he spent an entire season running around 20.5 and 20.6. Then came 20.40 at the Senior Federation Cup in 2025, followed by 20.32 at the Asian Championships.
Animesh Kujur won bronze medal in 200m at 2025 Asian Championships (Image credit: Special arrangement)
“So when it has to happen, it will happen,” he said. “No matter how much you push, the conditions should be like that, competition should be like that, and the atmosphere should be like that. And it's all about that day.”
There is a similar change in his 100m target.
The conversation around Kujur had once centred on whether he could break 10 seconds. Kujur has moved his own target further.
“No, I don't think of 10 flat, now I think of running 9,” he said.
Even after running 10.21, he felt there was more there.
“Even today, when I stood in 10.16, I thought, this is not a 10.16 race,” he said. “So it's okay, when it has to come, it comes.”
The lessons from his first international campaign
What matters now is getting the body to the right point. Kujur's first major international experience came at the 2025 Asian Championships, where he won bronze in the 200m. He says he was under pressure because he was representing India officially for the first time.
He does not expect that feeling to return in Japan.
“And the mistakes I made in the Asian Championships, I won't make again,” he said. “Because I was first international. Officially, I was representing India. And I was under pressure for that.”
Since then, he has raced at the World Championships, on the Continental Tour and at other international competitions. His coach has also encouraged him to use those races to experiment.
“With the upcoming LA Olympics, [the coaches have told me] don't miss any chance to make a mistake. And our ultimate aim is the LA Olympics,” Kujur said.
Learning when to push - and when to back off
The Asian Games therefore arrive after a season in which Kujur has learned more about managing the work around the races.
That will be particularly relevant in Aichi-Nagoya. Kujur says the heat and humidity will not be new to him.
“Yes, it is the same condition where I train. Same humidity, same heat,” he said. “And last time I competed in the World Championship. So I have an idea how to keep my body there and how to maintain things.”
“I know what form I am in, how my body is behaving, what time to take my body, when to peak, when to reduce the load, all the things that we have learned from the last year, how to maintain everything,” he said.
There is also a sizeable support system behind Kujur's preparation.
Animesh Kujur with Martin Owens (Image credit: Special arrangement)
“I have a lot of people on my support, like Reliance, Odisha Government, then TOPS, Athletic Federation of India, and others, and Puma, they never let me down,” he said. “Everyone wants me to improve, in every field, whether it's performance wise, or mental peace, or anything else. As a normal human being, everyone wants me to improve.”
The expectation he carries into his first Asian Games is also different from the one he had at the Asian Championships.
‘I know I am going to do well’
He has already won an Asian medal. He now wants to win one at a bigger multi-sport event.
“The success of the Asian Games will be a life-changing moment for me, because I have never won a medal in such a big game,” he said.
Asked which of the 100m, 200m and relay he considered his best medal opportunity, he did not pick one.
“Sure shot medal,” Kujur said. “I have won all three.”

stories.headline: Hockey India, franchises mull change in HIL governance structure
stories.deck: Even as some of the top brass of Hockey India was present in Chandigarh for the formal announcement of the men’s Asian Champions Trophy, HI president Dilip Tirkey was meeting Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and other senior government officials along with HIL franchises in New Delhi
stories.bodyText:
The tussle within Hockey India shows no sign of resolving any time soon.
Even as some of the top brass of the federation was present in Chandigarh for the formal announcement of the men’s Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) on Monday, president Dilip Tirkey was meeting Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and other senior government officials along with HIL franchises in New Delhi.
Sources said Tirkey introduced Ranjit Gill — Director of Hockey India and its senior most employee, her association with the sport going back decades — as the acting director general to everyone including the Minister. At the same time, Cdr R.K. Srivastava, who has been directed to cede authority as DG, was present along with secretary general Bholanath Singh and chief selector R.P. Singh in Chandigarh, accompanying Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann.
Monday’s meeting in New Delhi also saw concerns raised around the survival of the Hockey India League and its existing governance structure with Mandaviya making it clear in no uncertain terms that the government would back its continuation in every way.
Change in HIL ownership and governance structure
“The Minister assured full support to the HIL but also made it clear that the existing structure needed to be change. A five-member committee has been suggested including representatives from the franchises, Hockey India and the ministry to thrash out the best possible way forward,” sources in the know said.
There was also a proposal to make the franchise owners stakeholders in the league with a share of equity but there was disagreement about the percentage. While HI officials kept pushing for 51% and exclusive voting rights, the franchises present were keen on equitable holding, something the Ministry was more in favour of. The proposed committee has been asked to work out a framework within a month.
The Ministry has also reportedly assured Tirkey that its main interest was in ensuring the growth and development of hockey with no individual bigger than the sport and anyone unwilling was free to leave.
Batra, Asima in support
Meanwhile, former HI and FIH president Narinder Batra has thrown his support in Tirkey’s favour in the federation’s internal fight for control while suggesting measures to resolve the stalemate including constitution of an independent Ad Hoc Committee to oversee Hockey India until the elections, independently examining all POSH-related complaints, conducting an independent financial/forensic review of major expenditure, grants, benefits and payments among others.
“I understand that 12 Executive Board members have supported the position of Secretary General Bholanath Singh in relation to the proposed action concerning Cdr R.K. Srivastava. This development makes it even more important that the basis for these positions, and any relevant financial or other benefits provided to member units or individuals, are independently examined,” he said, referring to Tirkey’s notice of suspension to Srivastava.
Interestingly, two EB members — Asima Ali and and Sunil Malik — have declared their support for Tirkey as well. “I am writing this mail because I am really very upset after seeing that a person who is President of Hockey India, who has been a renowned player, a dignified person and a Member of Parliament and has always worked honestly for the development of hockey, is facing such opposition from the Executive Board.
“Rather these EB members are favouring a person (Director General) who has been continuously not complying with the orders of the president’s office. I am really surprised and disappointed to see all this and I do not support such behaviour where any official/EB member is disrespecting the chair and orders of president,” Asima wrote.
ACT from October 27
Meanwhile in Chandigarh, Mann released the tournament logo for the October 27-November 5 event with the league matches in Jalandhar and the knockouts and final in Mohali. The six nation tournament — including Pakistan, Malaysia, Korea, Japan and China — has been made ticket-free with the India-Pakistan clash scheduled for November 1. Oman and Bangladesh are the reserve teams.
The two venues — Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar and ₹8.96 crore for the Olympian Balbir Singh (Senior) International Hockey Stadium in Mohali — will be upgraded at a coast of ₹14 crore and ₹8.96 crore respectively. “These are not merely infrastructure projects but an investment in Punjab’s sporting future,” Mann added, declaring that the event would be a testing ground for the state staking its claim to host the 2030 World Cup as well.

stories.headline: Leeds crushes Newcastle; Roma and Inter stay tied atop Serie A
stories.deck: Betis’ fairy tale start to the Spanish season continued with victory over Villarreal.
stories.bodyText:
Leeds hammered woeful Newcastle 4-1 to go third in the Premier League on Monday (September 14, 2026) while Real Betis won 2-1 at Villarreal to move equal on points with second-place Real Madrid in La Liga.
The top two in Italy, Roma and Inter Milan, won comfortably to maintain their 100% records and Como beat Parma 2-1 to climb into third spot.
Betis’ fairy tale start to the Spanish season continued with victory over Villarreal.
The win, courtesy of goals from Cucho Hernández and Natan, came 10 days after it beat Real Madrid 1-0 in La Liga, and less than a week after it overcame Lille 3-2 in its first Champions League group match since 2005.
The result at Estadio de la Ceramica lifts Betis into second place, tied with Madrid on 12 points. Barcelona is top on 15.
It was another disappointing night for the home side, which is still to win this season and sits third-bottom with two points from five matches.
In Italy, Roma continued its superb start to the season with a 2-0 win over Torino. It was joined at the top of the table by the only other team with maximum points, Inter Milan, which came from behind to crush Udinese 5-3.
Both teams have 12 points from four games, although Roma is first on goal difference after what was its ninth consecutive victory.
In-form striker Donyell Malen scored his sixth goal in four games to put Roma ahead and Niccolò Pisilli got a deserved second in stoppage time.
Inter struggled to get going against Udinese, which looked set to continue its good run of away form by scoring twice without reply in the opening 16 minutes.
James Abankwah rose unmarked to head Udinese ahead in the ninth minute and Jurgen Ekkelenkamp doubled its lead seven minutes later.
However, Carlos Augusto got a goal back for the reigning champion after 26 minutes with a 30-yard strike and Nicolo Barella equalized 10 minutes before half time.
Marcus Thuram, Francesco Pio Esposito and Ange-Yoan Bonny scored in a commanding second half, and although Idrissa Gueye grabbed a third for Udinese in stoppage time it was nowhere near enough for the visitor.
In Como, the home side moved into the top three with a 2-1 win over Parma.
Jacobo Ramon turned Nico Paz’s shot in for the opener midway through the first half and Kaiki made it 2-0 seven minutes from time after a goalmouth scramble. Jose David Romero got Parma’s consolation in stoppage time.
Como is third on 10 points along with Lazio.
In England, Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the star man as Leeds overran a flimsy Newcastle side.
The home team turned it on during a sparkling first half and took the lead in the 32nd minute when Ao Tanaka’s shot from the edge of the box took a double deflection to bamboozle Newcastle keeper Lukas Hornicek.
Three minutes later, sloppy defending led to Calvert-Lewin making a second with a trademark header, the goal being marked down to Jayden Bogle after the ball went in off his head.
Calvert-Lewin then grabbed his fourth goal in four games on the stroke of half time. Noah Okafor rounded off the scoring for Leeds with a half volley after another weak clearance early in the second period.
Newcastle’s consolation goal came in the final minute from substitute Bazoumana Touré.
The result lifts Leeds into third place in the Premier League, equal with Hull on eight points, four behind joint leaders Arsenal and Manchester City. Newcastle is 12th.

stories.headline: Ronaldo leads Al Nassr back to Asia’s top table after a year in the second tier
stories.deck: Cristiano Ronaldo and Al Nassr return to the AFC Champions League Elite after winning the Saudi Pro League and spending last season in the second-tier competition. Their campaign begins against Al Ain, who eliminated them in 2024. With new manager Ange Postecoglou and a revamped squad, Al Nassr are chasing continental glory as Ronaldo seeks his first major Asian club trophy.
stories.bodyText:
Cristiano Ronaldo
 is back where he believes Al Nassr belong. After spending last season in Asia’s second-tier competition, the Saudi giants return to the AFC Champions League Elite on Tuesday, with Ronaldo once again chasing the one major continental club trophy that has eluded him since moving to the Middle East. Their opening assignment is a familiar one: Al Ain, the same UAE club that ended Al Nassr’s 
Champions League
 run in 2024. But this is a very different Al Nassr, with a league title, a new manager and a revamped continental competition waiting for them.
Why are Al Nassr back in the AFC Champions League Elite?
Al Nassr's absence from the top tier last season was not a permanent step down. The Riyadh club failed to qualify for the 2025–26 AFC Champions League Elite and instead competed in the second-tier AFC Champions League Two, where they eventually lost the final to Japan's Gamba Osaka.
Their route back was secured by winning the 2025–26 Saudi Pro League, ending a seven-year wait for the domestic title. Al Nassr finished two points ahead of Al-Hilal, with Ronaldo scoring twice in a 4-1 final-day victory over Damac to seal the championship.
The title also brought a significant change on the touchline. Jorge Jesus departed after leading Al Nassr to the league crown, and the club appointed Ange Postecoglou on a two-year contract. 
The former Tottenham and Celtic manager had already won the UEFA Europa League with Spurs and brings previous Asian experience from his time with Australia and Yokohama F. Marinos.
So, after playing in the secondary competition last season, Al Nassr are back in the continent's premier club tournament for 2026–27.
What has changed in the AFC Champions League Elite?
Ronaldo's return comes in the first season of a major expansion to the competition.
The 2026–27 AFC Champions League Elite has grown from 24 clubs to 32, split evenly between the West and East regions. Each region contains 16 teams, with every club playing eight league-stage matches: Four at home and four away, against eight different opponents.
There are no traditional groups. Instead, all 16 clubs in each region are ranked in a single league table, with the top eight from each region advancing to the knockout stage.
The round of 16 remains regional and is played over two legs, but the competition then moves to a centralised Finals in Saudi Arabia. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final will be staged there, with the final scheduled for May 1, 2027.
For Al Nassr, the West Region is packed with familiar Saudi opposition. They are joined by Al-Hilal, Al-Ahli, Al-Ittihad and Al-Qadsiah, alongside clubs including Al Ain and Shabab Al Ahli from the UAE, Qatar's Al Sadd, Al Gharafa and Al Shamal, Iran's Esteghlal and Tractor, Uzbekistan's Pakhtakor and Neftchi, and Iraq's Air Force Club.
What is Cristiano Ronaldo's Champions League record with Al Nassr?
Ronaldo has already played a significant role in Al Nassr's recent continental campaigns, although he has never taken the club all the way to the title.
His first top-tier AFC Champions League campaign came in 2023–24, when Al Nassr reached the quarter-finals before losing to Al Ain on penalties. Ronaldo scored six goals in that tournament.
He returned for the 2024–25 AFC Champions League Elite, when Al Nassr went further, reaching the semi-finals. Ronaldo scored eight goals, including against Al Ain in the league stage and in the quarter-final victory over Yokohama F. Marinos. The AFC confirmed he had reached eight goals in the competition after scoring in the 4-1 quarter-final win.
That gives Ronaldo a top-tier record of 14 goals in 16 appearances for Al Nassr across those two campaigns.
Last season was different. Ronaldo appeared four times in the AFC Champions League Two, scoring once, as Al Nassr's continental campaign moved into the second tier.
Now, at 41, he returns to the competition that matters most in Asia, and he does so having already won Champions League titles in Europe with Manchester United and Real Madrid.
Who do Al Nassr play and what are their chances?
The comeback begins against Al Ain on Tuesday, September 15, at the Hazza bin Zayed Stadium, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm local time.
It is a particularly interesting opening fixture because Al Ain are not an unfamiliar opponent. They eliminated Al Nassr in the 2023–24 quarter-finals, winning the tie on penalties after the two legs finished level on aggregate.
The UAE side arrive with their own credentials, having completed a domestic double without losing a league match. They therefore represent a serious test immediately rather than a gentle introduction to the expanded competition.
Al Nassr, meanwhile, have plenty of attacking firepower. Ronaldo is joined by Sadio Mané, João Félix and Kingsley Coman, while Postecoglou is now tasked with translating last season's domestic success into continental progress.
There is also unfinished business. Al Nassr have yet to win Asia's premier club competition during Ronaldo's time at the club, despite reaching the quarter-finals and then the semi-finals in his previous two top-tier campaigns. The club's loss to Gamba Osaka in last season's AFC Champions League Two final only added another painful continental chapter.
This time, they return to the top table with a Saudi title behind them, a new manager in charge and Ronaldo once again leading the pursuit of a trophy he has never won in Asia.

briefs.headline: Asia Cup trophy row: BCCI's Rajeev Shukla says Naqvi did not raise any objection on ‘collective decision’
briefs.deck: On images showing Devajit Saikia talking to Mohsin Naqvi during the Asia Cup final, the BCCI Vice-President said it was a mere “routine interaction”
briefs.bodyText:
BCCI Vice-President Rajeev Shukla on Monday (September 14, 2026) said Indian women team’s refusal to accept the Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi was Board’s “collective decision" and the Asian Cricket Council chairperson also "did not raise any objection" to it.
India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday (September 13, 2026) in Dubai but did not accept the trophy from Mr. Naqvi, continuing a trend started by the men's team during the 2025 Asia Cup following last year's Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people.
“We discussed the matter among ourselves and decided that we would not accept it (trophy) from him. It was our collective decision. He (Naqvi) also did not raise any objection to it,” Mr. Shukla told reporters after arriving at the Indira Gandhi International Airport with the team.
“We informed our team accordingly, and he presented it to whoever he had to and then left,” Shukla added.
The veteran administrator’s words mirrored the stance of BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia.
“We had taken a conscious decision considering all prevailing aspects, and our position had been communicated to the ACC in advance, that the Indian team would not participate in the trophy presentation under the circumstances,” Mr. Saikia had told PTI earlier.
Some images had surfaced earlier of Mr. Saikia talking to Mr. Naqvi during the Asia Cup final, but Mr. Shukla said it was a mere “routine interaction.” “What Saikia ji said is absolutely correct. When you are at a match, everyone is present there and interacts in a professional capacity. Therefore, I do not think there should be so much criticism over that,” he said.
Mr. Shukla also congratulated the team on the Asia Cup triumph, and expressed confidence in the team doing well in the upcoming Asian Games in Japan.
“We became Asia Cup champions. Our women have once again made us proud and we will continue to win in the future.
“The team is now heading to Japan and we are fully confident that we will secure a victory there as well,” he said.

briefs.headline: Equestrian Agarwalla gives up Asian Games fight; feels 'betrayed' by Sports Ministry
briefs.deck: Equestrian Anush Agarwalla conceded his dream of competing in the 2026 Asian Games, which begin on September 19, is over. The rider said he felt 'betrayed' after his pleas to the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Sports Ministry and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) went unheard.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Equestrian 
Anush Agarwalla
 conceded his dream of competing in the 2026 
Asian Games
, which begin on September 19, is over. The rider said he felt 'betrayed' after his pleas to the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Sports Ministry and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) went unheard.
"The dream of Asian Games 2026 is officially over. Words cannot explain the pain and emptiness I feel right now. I have always represented India with immense pride, and always will. But this time, I am deeply hurt - not because I lost, but because I was never given the chance to compete," he wrote in a post.
"I can accept defeat on the field. That is sport. You fight, you win, you lose, and you come back stronger. But this feels less like defeat and more like betrayal. Accepting an outcome doesn't mean I have to believe the process was right.
"I fought until the very last moment, and I am proud of that. A fight for a medal is any day a better fight. A fight against the system may never yield a medal, but at least it leaves a record of who stood in the way between me, Floriana, my horse, and the medal we worked for. Maybe I didn't get to fight for the medal. But I made sure the message was registered. 
Despite reaching out to the Federation, IOA and the Ministry, there was no effort to review what happened. I only hope no athlete has to go through this again. If India wants to become a true sporting nation, athletes deserve a system that is fair, transparent and respects the years of work behind every opportunity," he continued.
In July, the Supreme Court had dismissed riders Agarwalla and Sudipti Hajela's pleas challenging the Delhi High Court’s refusal to interfere with their non-selection in the dressage team for the Asian Games.
A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe had refused to grant any relief to the two-time Asian Games medallist, saying the court is very reluctant to interfere in individual sports matters.
Both riders won gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games and had filed petitions after they were not selected for the upcoming edition by the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI).
In August, the Sports Ministry had stressed that it would stick to the selection criterias despite "pressure being created."
Image credit: Anush Agarwalla's Instagram handle
In its selection criteria unveiled in 2025, the Ministry had made it clear that only those with "realistic chance of winning a medal" would be considered for multi-sport events, including the Asian Games, through selection trials that would be videographed and overseen by independent observers.
EFI's ad-hoc committee had first named a selection list in June for the dressage event at the Asian Games, where Agarwalla and Hajela were placed as reserve riders. Agarwalla was named as first reserve and Hajela as second reserve — while four riders were selected ahead of them (Shruti Vora, Gaurav Pundir, Jai Sud and Hriday Chheda).
The Asian Games will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan from September 19 to October 4.

briefs.headline: Varun Chakaravarthy ruled out of Afghanistan series due to injury
briefs.deck: With the Asian Games in Japan starting soon after, it isn’t yet clear whether Varun’s injury will rule him out of the multi-sport spectacle too.
briefs.bodyText:
Spinner Varun Chakaravarthy has been ruled out of India’s next two T20Is against Afghanistan in the national capital on Tuesday and Thursday. The 35-year-old is understood to have developed a side strain after featuring in the Men in Blue’s seven-wicket win in the opener on Sunday (September 13, 2026). He had returned figures of 4-0-16-1.
“Varun has suffered an injury. He will play no further part in the series,” a source told The Hindu on Monday (September 14, 2026).
With the Asian Games in Japan starting soon after, it isn’t yet clear whether Varun’s injury will rule him out of the multi-sport spectacle too.
Varun has had an injury-marred year. After suffering a hairline fracture in his left foot during the Indian Premier League, he also hurt his hamstring and returned early from India’s T20 series against England in the United Kingdom. He missed the subsequent three-match series against Zimbabwe.
Interestingly, the mystery spinner from Tamil Nadu had appeared in the post-match press conference on Sunday, and provided no inkling of his latest injury during the interaction. Asked about his mindset whilst on the treatment table, he had said: “Injuries are common for sportspersons. It just shows that we are giving our best. Sometimes we push beyond our limits and that is when the body gives in. So that is when we have to take a step back, work better and come back stronger.”

briefs.headline: South Korea coach denies ‘extreme’ ChatGPT reliance after former club sacked him
briefs.deck: Robert Moreno has denied claims that he used artificial intelligence to prepare for matches during his time at Russian club Sochi. The new South Korea interim coach called the reports false and said his use of technology was taken out of context. Moreno is now focused on rebuilding confidence in the national team, with Son Heung-min remaining captain.
briefs.bodyText:
Robert Moreno has walked into one of the more demanding jobs in international football with South Korea desperate to rebuild confidence, but his first press conference quickly turned towards an unusual controversy from his previous role. The Spaniard was forced to address claims that artificial intelligence had played an inappropriate role in his work at Russian club Sochi, before turning his attention to a very different challenge: restoring belief in the Taegeuk Warriors.
Robert Moreno denies using AI to prepare for games
Moreno strongly denied reports that he relied heavily on artificial intelligence during his time at Sochi, where he was dismissed in September 2025 following a poor start to the season.
The Spaniard took charge of the Russian Premier League club on December 15, 2023, arriving with Sochi at the bottom of the table. He remained in the job until September 2, 2025, when he left by mutual consent after the club collected just one point from its opening seven matches of the new campaign. His overall record at Sochi ended with 22 wins, 17 draws and 23 defeats.
The controversy surrounding his methods emerged after his departure. 
Sochi's former sporting and general director Andrei Orlov claimed Moreno had developed an unusually heavy reliance on ChatGPT for a wide range of club operations.
According to claims from club officials, AI was allegedly used for everything from planning training sessions and identifying potential transfer targets to selecting starting lineups and organising travel. One particularly controversial example involved an away trip to Khabarovsk, where an AI-generated itinerary reportedly proposed keeping the players awake for 28 consecutive hours.
The claims also included an alleged recommendation involving striker Artur Shushenachev, further fuelling suggestions that ChatGPT had gone far beyond being a simple analytical tool and had become involved in key football decisions.
Moreno rejected that portrayal when the subject was raised at his first press conference as South Korea's interim coach in Cheonan on Monday.
“It was a piece of news that is completely false and went viral,” he said.
Moreno acknowledged that he does use technology but insisted that the reports had distorted how he worked.
“Obviously I use technology,” he said. “If you verify facts, you will see that much of what was reported was taken out of context and blown out of proportion.”
He added: “Anyone who spends 10 minutes looking into it can see that everything has been taken out of context and put together to cause harm.”
Moreno was appointed South Korea's interim coach in August on a contract running until the end of November. The Korea Football Association could extend that arrangement through the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January and February, although that would be “subject to an evaluation”.
The 48-year-old, who previously took charge of Spain for nine matches in 2009, is the first Spaniard to coach South Korea.
Son Heung-min remains captain as Moreno names first squad
Moreno's first assignment is to prepare South Korea for a series of friendlies, beginning with Ecuador on September 24.
Son Heung-min remains captain after being included in Moreno's first squad. The 34-year-old LAFC forward remains a central figure for a national team attempting to recover from a disappointing World Cup campaign
Moreno highlighted the veteran's versatility when discussing his plans.
“We're all aware of Son's versatility,” he said. “For me he can play in three positions.”
Moreno also used his first appearance before the Korean media to promise a more positive experience for supporters.
“We're going to try to do our work honestly and with the aim of making all Korean football fans happy,” he said.
His appointment followed the resignation of Hong Myung-bo, who stepped down after South Korea were eliminated in the group stage of the World Cup.
Moreno is therefore taking over a team whose problems have extended well beyond results, with public confidence in the national side and the country's football authorities both badly damaged.
South Korea's football leadership has endured a turbulent period
Discontent surrounding Hong's appointment in 2024 had already caused anger among supporters, but the World Cup disappointment intensified the scrutiny.
Hong was questioned by lawmakers at a parliamentary hearing in July alongside Chung Mong-gyu, the former head of the Korea Football Association. The KFA's offices were subsequently raided by police in August.
The federation also apologised after a leaked government audit reported that it had provided “sexual entertainment” for foreign referees in 2011 and 2012.
Moreno has made clear that he does not intend to publicly dissect Hong's tenure, despite having studied the team's World Cup performances closely.
“I have studied World Cup matches and players inside out but I think it is inappropriate to publicly evaluate my predecessor,” he said.
Instead, Moreno wants the previous failures to become something the team can learn from.
“It is important to use whatever happened in the past as a learning opportunity,” he added. “What is clear is that when you lose, many problems surface. But when you win, they fade away.”
For now, Moreno has six matches to work with before the end of his initial contract. After Ecuador, South Korea are scheduled to face Uruguay, Venezuela and Uzbekistan, along with two opponents yet to be named, as preparations build towards the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia.

briefs.headline: 'I don’t even know if I’ll be there': ICC No.2 Steve Smith uncertain over Ashes 2027
briefs.deck: Steve Smith has voiced hesitation about his involvement in the 2027 Ashes series as he evaluates his Test career after each series. Although winning an Ashes series in England is a significant goal for him, his main focus is now on competing for Australia at the 2028 Olympics. To achieve this, Smith is engaging actively in T20 cricket to hone his skills.
briefs.bodyText:
Steve Smith has admitted he is not certain whether he will still be playing Test cricket when Australia travel to England for the 2027 Ashes, raising fresh questions over the future of one of Australia's greatest modern batters.
The 37-year-old is taking his Test career series by series and has refused to set a retirement date. While the prospect of finally winning an Ashes series in England remains an attraction, Smith acknowledged that he could walk away from Test cricket before next summer's series.
“I don’t even know if I’ll be there yet,” Smith told The Telegraph when asked about the 2027 Ashes.
Smith keeps retirement decision open
Smith has made it clear that he is not thinking too far ahead with his Test career. Instead, the Australian batter is assessing his motivation and energy after each series.
“I’m kind of a series-by-series proposition, as I’ve been for a while,” he said.
Smith has already enjoyed an extraordinary Test career, featuring in 125 Tests and scoring 37 centuries. He is also currently ranked second among men's Test batters, behind England's Harry Brook. Despite his age, Smith said he is still enjoying playing cricket and has no fixed retirement date.
“I’ve achieved a lot in the game. It’s been a great ride for the last 15 years or thereabouts. I’ve had a lot of fun. I’m still enjoying it, so I don’t have an end date, we’ll wait and see,” he said.
Winning an Ashes series in England still on his list
One of the few major achievements missing from Smith's illustrious career is winning an Ashes series outright in England. Australia retained the Ashes during Smith's tours in 2019 and 2023, with both series ending 2-2. However, Australia have not won an Ashes series in England since 2001.
Smith admitted that winning the Ashes in England would be special, but the possibility of achieving that goal is not enough for him to commit to playing in 2027.
“I’d love to win one there or to have won one there, but you wait and see if that comes to fruition,” he said.
Smith turns his attention to LA 2028 Olympics
Rather than making the 2027 Ashes his main long-term target, Smith revealed that his biggest ambition at this stage of his career is to represent Australia at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Cricket will return to the Olympic programme at LA 2028 in the T20 format, giving Smith another reason to continue developing his game in the shortest format.
The Australian is currently playing for the Amsterdam Flames in the European T20 Premier League, with Smith saying that one of his motivations for joining the competition was to play more T20 cricket.
“Right now probably it’s just the Olympics to try to be a part of that,” Smith said.
Australia will travel to South Africa for a three-game Test series in October, which is Smith’s first Test trip to the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal that led to his 12-month ban from international cricket.
“Oh, for me, it’s just another series. All that happened a long time ago, and we’ve played a lot of cricket – we’ve been back to South Africa since then for one-dayers. They’re a good side at the moment – obviously beat us in the World Test Championship final. They have a really good pace attack as well, so should be a cracker of a series.”
